blocks.text: MANILA – Few tropical cyclones are expected to develop or enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) in the last quarter of the year, but some could intensify into typhoons or super typhoons. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) is expecting one to two tropical cyclones each for October, November and December. “Few tropical cyclones are expected in the last quarter, especially amid the El Niño,” PAGASA Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section chief Ana Liza Solis said in a radio interview. She said most of the potential cyclones are landfalling and crossing types. READ: Inday rainfall helpful for […]...
